subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — NovaHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dubois <alex.dubois@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — Dedicated capacity, isolation, and scaling (NovaHealth)

Alex / Maya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain points (what you told us):
- Production latency spikes during peak clinical-hours (avg P95 jumps from 120ms -> 400ms).
- Strict data isolation and audit requirements for PHI-preserving pipelines (cannot share inference workload with other customers).
- Need for predictable capacity for batch overnight jobs and burst handling during launches.

Goals you outlined:
- Move to dedicated GPU capacity (reserved pool) with private networking for PHI-compliant inference.
- Achieve sustained P95 < 150ms for live API routes and SLA-backed availability for the inference service.
- Autoscaling policy that supports scheduled nightly batch windows and on-demand burst for product launches.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated configuration (high-level):
- Reserved pool: 8 x A100 (or equivalent) dedicated GPUs to start (handles current steady-state + 2x burst headroom).
- Private deployment: VPC peering, KMS-managed keys, and audit log streaming to your SIEM.
- Scaling: configured autoscaling policy for scheduled scale-up to +4 GPUs overnight and manual burst capacity for launches.
- SLA targets: 99.9% monthly uptime for the dedicated pool, with P95 latency SLO of 150ms for the production model.

Next steps (requested items):
1) We’ll share a draft SOW and capacity diagram for your infra team to review (attached).
2) Can you confirm the expected qps during peak clinical hours and the size of your nightly batch window? (we estimated 1.8–2.5k qps peak).
3) Please loop in procurement for contract/term questions — I’ve added placeholder DocuSign link below when you’re ready.

Attachments: novahealth-sow-draft.pdf (SOW draft), capacity-diagram.png (high level network & topology)

I’ll follow up with a more detailed cost/throughput estimate once we get your peak qps numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Dubois <alex.dubois@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated capacity, isolation, and scaling (NovaHealth)

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak qps: we’re seeing 2,200 qps sustained during morning clinical hours (08:00–10:00 local). On product launch days, short bursts up to ~4,500 qps for ~5–10 minutes.
- Nightly batch: 02:00–05:00 local, ~6M tokens/day across the batch jobs.
- Isolation: we need single-tenant GPUs (no co-tenancy) and SOC 2 evidence for audit teams.

On the SOW — procurement will want term options (12 vs 24 months) and a clear SLA credit table. Can you add the SLA credit terms to the SOW?

Also, can Dylan or someone on the infra team confirm how the KV cache warmup would impact cold-start latency? I’m cc’ing Maya (infra) and procurement.

Appreciate it — Alex
CTO, NovaHealth
alex.dubois@novahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dubois <alex.dubois@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated capacity, isolation, and scaling (NovaHealth)

Thanks Alex — helpful numbers. Key responses below and next actions: 

1) Term options & SLA credits: noted. I’ll add 12/24 month pricing tables and a detailed SLA credit schedule to the SOW. Expect the updated draft by EOD.

2) Peak/burst sizing: given 2.2k sustained qps and 4.5k short bursts, our recommendation is to start with 8 dedicated A100s + burst capacity of 4 additional A100s (pre-warmed on demand). This gives headroom and keeps steady-state unit cost economical.

3) Nightly batch sizing: we’ll model the 6M token window against a scheduled scale-up (02:00–05:00) — will include estimated run-time and cost in the updated doc.

4) SOC 2 & evidence: attaching our SOC 2 summary page in the SOW; Dylan will follow up with the audit artifact links and logging configuration.

Next actions for you: please confirm the QPS buckets below so we can finalize the cost model:
- sustained peak: 2200 qps
- burst peak: 4500 qps (5–10 minutes)
- batch: 6M tokens nightly (02:00–05:00)

I’ll send the updated SOW + price table + SLA schedule this afternoon.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dubois <alex.dubois@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated capacity, isolation, and scaling (NovaHealth)

Alex / Maya — quick technical notes on cold-start / KV cache and isolation:

- Cold-starts & KV warmup: If you pre-warm KV caches for your most common prefixes (we can provide a warmup script), cold-start latency for a warmed model should be under 100ms P95. For fully cold KV caches, expect an initial P95 up to ~350–450ms for the first few requests while KV pages are populated. We recommend keeping a small always-on pool for latency-sensitive routes to avoid cold penalty.

- Isolation: Redwood Dedicated supports single-tenant GPU pools with VPC-only access and KMS integration; audit logs can be pushed to your CloudWatch/Datadog or S3 bucket. We’ll include a diagram of the networking boundaries in the capacity-diagram.png.

- Autoscaling policy suggestion: scheduled scale to +4 GPUs (02:00–05:30) for batch; reactive burst policy with pre-warm TTL of 10 minutes to handle short spikes.

I’ll attach the warmup script and a short runbook once Marissa finalizes the SOW. Happy to jump on a 30-minute technical sync with your infra team if helpful.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
